newsitem.title: UK: Arrests and bomb alert after N. Irish man wounded.
newsitem.headline: Arrests and bomb alert after N. Irish man wounded.

text.p: Several people were arrested in a rural Northern Irish town on Thursday after a 19-year-old man was seriously wounded in what residents said appeared to be a British military undercover operation.
A security source said the arrests in Coalisland, County Tyrone followed the incident late on Wednesday.
Police said a British army bomb disposal officer was later sent to a housing estate behind the town's police station.
"A number of home have been evacuated," a police spokesman said. He was unable to say whether the officer had been summoned because of a specific alert or as a precaution.

The incidents coincided with heightened tension in the province where Irish Republican Army guerrillas have launched a series of attacks on British security forces and a truce by pro-British Loyalist extremists is fragile.
The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule, is suspected of carrying out two bomb attacks that disrupted rail services in northwestern England on Thursday.
Despite the bombs, Irish security sources do not rule out a fresh IRA truce, an Irish newspaper said Thursday.
"Security sources hopeful of new IRA ceasefire," the Irish Times newspaper said in a front-page article.

The paper said political activists had regained lost ground within the so-called Republican Movement, which embraces the IRA and its Sinn Fein political arm, and that guerrillas might move to get Sinn Fein into talks with Britain.

Police said details of the Coalisland shooting incident were sketchy. A man had been taken to hospital and an investigation was under way. They could not say what had caused a blast heard in the area. A hostile crowd had gathered at the scene, they said.
Local people said they suspected an explosion, heard shortly before 10 p.m. (2200 GMT), was caused by a stun grenade fired by security forces.
The wounded man underwent emergency surgency for a stomach wound, said Robert Sowney, a spokesman for South Tyrone Hospital. "His condition is ill but stable," he told Reuters.
Municipal councillor Jim Canning said he was at a function nearby in the town.

"There was an explosion followed by a number of gunshots. Some of us went outside and there was a man lying on the ground surrounded by a number of men who appeared to be some form of undercover operation," he told reporters.

Television journalist Paul Clark, who had been at an event in the town, said: "I saw a guy lying on the ground with his hands tied behind his back. He was being manhandled by a number of men who were kneeling beside him. They were wearing civilian clothes.
"One of them had a hat with the word army' on it. He was armed," Clark told Reuters.
"A number of cars drove up the street very quickly... A number of men got out, in civilian clothes wearing hats with army' on them. They were armed. They spoke with English accents.
"Before they and the ambulance left, they fired a number of shots in the air. They seemed to let off firecrackers to disperse a rather large crowd that had arrived...and then they drove off."
